The Newsroom That Still Meets at Noon | Meridian Review
The Newsroom That Still Meets at Noon
Four editors, one table, and a paper that goes to print whether they agree or not.

At five to twelve the chairs start to scrape. Nobody is called; nobody has been called in thirty years. The four of them sit where they always sit, and tomorrow's front page goes in the middle of the table.
The rule is older than any of them. Whatever is on the table at noon is what the town reads in the morning. You can argue until then. After that you can only sharpen.
Most papers this size gave up the daily meeting when the newsroom emptied out. This one kept the meeting and let the rest go: no office hours, no desks by the window, just a table and a clock.
It is not efficient. It is the only part of the day when everyone who decides what counts is looking at the same sheet of paper.

Do my files stay on my computer?
Yes. Your library, collections, and covers are saved on your Mac, and articles are turned into Kindle books there too. There is no Dispatch account and no Dispatch server.

The Chrome extension hands a page straight to the app on your Mac. An article leaves your Mac only when you send it, from your own email account to your Kindle. If you turn on drawn covers, the title and a short summary go to OpenAI under your own key.
How do I set up my Kindle?
Paste your Kindle's email address, the one ending in @kindle.com. Find My Kindle Email opens the Amazon page that shows it.
Choose the email account Dispatch sends from (Gmail, iCloud, Outlook, Yahoo, Fastmail, or another) and enter an app password for it. The password is kept in your Keychain.
On that same Amazon page, add your email address to the Approved Personal Document E-mail List. Amazon rejects anything sent from an address that isn't on it.
Is it a native Mac app?

Yes. Dispatch for Mac is built for macOS 26 Tahoe, and every window and control is SwiftUI. The sidebar, toolbar, menus, and Settings behave like the rest of your Mac, and passwords and keys live in the Keychain.
